story_type: NASA drone engineer rides the back seat of an F/A-18, cockpit camera, greeted on landing
hook: He builds a drone with no pilot. Today he flew in a fighter jet.
narration: He builds systems for a drone with no pilot on board. Today he rode in a fighter jet.
Russell Franz is a lead engineer on NASA's Global Hawk drone at Edwards, California.
NASA's Administrator set up these rides to reward people for their work.
The F/A-18 rolled down the runway and lifted off, with a camera pointed at him the whole time.
In hard turns, riders squeeze their legs and stomach as hard as they can. That keeps blood in the brain, so they stay awake.
Then the horizon tipped on its side, again and again.
[short pause] Back on the ground, people were waiting for him on the flight line.
outcome: Russell Franz landed safely, climbed down from the jet and got a big hug on the flight line.
title: Drone engineer's first fighter jet ride
description:
On Oct. 8, 2026, Russell Franz, a development lead on NASA's Global Hawk project, rode in the back seat of an F/A-18 at NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, as part of the agency's employee incentive flights.
